page0.text:
...Right.
If I burst into the room while Sakura's changing, I won't hear the end of it from Fuji-nee for an entire year.

page1.text:
"No, the point is that it would be wrong to do that to Sakura!"
Yup, now is the time for patience.
For all I know, she could already be done and drying her hair off.

page2.text:
"You look unsettled, Shirou."
"Huh? N-no I don't. I'm eating mandarins and drinking tea."
"Haah. You've barely laid a hand on the fruit or tea, and you keep glancing at the clock. Is that what you call resting?"

page3.text:
"Oof. Well, I'm full, so I don't have much of an appetite."
"Indeed? If you say so, Shirou. I don't believe in excessive self-restraint, however."

page4.text:
Saber takes a graceful sip of tea.
...God, I'm pathetic.
It hasn't even been five minutes, but I can't stop thinking about Sakura.

page5.text:
"Damn it, I don't care what Fuji-nee says!
Saber, I'm going to the bathroom!"
I grit my teeth and stand up.
Just as I do,
Fuji-nee comes hurtling out of the hallway.

page6.text:
"Fuji-nee...? What's the rush? Weren't you getting Sakura's clothes ready?"
"I just finished. Never mind that, Shirou. Look after Sakura. I'm going home to get some fever medication."
"!? What do you mean? What happened?"

page7.text: "I wish I knew. I found Sakura collapsed on the floor of the dressing room, and her temperature was almost 38 degrees."

page8.text:
"Wha—Sakura collapsed!?"
"She's sleeping in the guestroom now. It looks like she only caught a cold, you can relax.
But don't let her push herself. I'll bring a bunch of stuff from home, so you stay with her. That alone will make Sakura feel better."

page9.text:
Fuji-nee snaps off a series of orders, then heads home to the Fujimura estate.
Fuji-nee's house hosts a lot of young, hot-blooded people, so it's well-equipped to handle the sick and wounded.

page10.text:
"Argh...!"
I can't freeze now.
I don't know what happened, but I need to check on Sakura first!

page11.text:
"Your fever's a tad over 37 degrees. Huh. That's lower than I expected."
I shake the thermometer and look at Sakura, who's lying in bed.
It's been thirty minutes.
Like Fuji-nee said, Sakura's condition isn't too serious. It seems like she passed out in the dressing room because she had a light cold, took a long bath, and got lightheaded when she stood up.

page12.text:
"I'm sorry... I must have gotten dizzy after getting into the bath in such a nervous state."
Sakura guiltily hides her face under the covers.

page13.text:
"Well, there's no helping the fact that you're sick. A cold like this should heal with medicine and some rest, so try and take it easy for tonight.
I'll leave water on this chair. Try not to go outside, all right? You'll get a chill."
Just in case, I put on another blanket over her and turn off the lights.

page14.text:
"See ya tomorrow. I'll come wake you up, so take it easy."
I give Sakura an affectionate pat on the head and make for the door.
"...Okay. Good night, Senpai."
Sakura sounds apologetic.
I reciprocate her good-night, and leave the guestroom.
